what.question: What is Jack Fix It?
what.answer: An app for home services. You tell Jack what's going on at home, pros near you answer with fixed-price quotes, and you choose the one that fits. Booking, payment, chat and the job's progress all stay in the app.

cost.question: Does it cost anything to ask for quotes?
cost.answer: No. Sending a request and getting quotes is free. You pay only when you accept a quote, and you see the total, with any tax, before you confirm it.

paid.question: When does the pro get paid?
paid.answer: After the job, through the app. Once the pro marks the work as done, you confirm the job in the app.

methods.question: How can I pay?
methods.answer: By card, or with Apple Pay or Google Pay where your phone offers them. The payment runs on Stripe's secure checkout, so Jack Fix It never stores your card number.

verified.question: How are pros verified?
verified.answer: Before a pro can send you a quote, our team reviews the information and documents they provide and approves their profile. You'll see the green seal next to a verified pro's name.

privacy.question: Who can see my contact details and address?
privacy.answer: Pros never see your phone number or email. Before you book, they see only your city and ZIP code; the pro you book gets the full address to do the job. To talk, you both use the chat.

languages.question: Which languages is the app in?
languages.answer: English and Spanish. You choose the language in the app's settings.

available.question: When can I get the app?
available.answer: Soon. We're getting it ready for iPhone and Android, and the download links will be on this page.

joinPro.question: I'm a pro. How do I join?
joinPro.answer: You'll create your pro profile in the app: your categories, the ZIP codes you cover, your documents and your payout account. Our team reviews every profile before it starts getting requests.

firstResponse.title: First response
firstResponse.description: Mean time from a new request to the BDC's first contact.

repeatRate.title: Repeat rate
repeatRate.description: Customers who came back for another job.

formula.first_response_minutes: Requests created in the range that have a first contact by the BDC: the mean and the median of the time from the request to that first contact. Counted: those requests.
formula.contact_rate: Requests created in the range that have a first contact (made at any time since) ÷ requests created in the range.
formula.lead_to_job: Requests created in the range that have a job, whatever its status ÷ requests created in the range.
formula.completion_rate: Jobs created in the range (paid and scheduled) that reached “completed” ÷ jobs created in the range. A job that was confirmed, paid out, disputed or refunded passed through “completed” and counts. A job cancelled before it started counts only below the line.
formula.customer_rating: The mean overall rating (1–5) of the reviews pros wrote about their customers in the range, published or not.
formula.pro_rating: The mean overall rating (1–5) of the reviews customers wrote about their pros in the range, published or not.
formula.dispute_rate: Problems reported (disputes opened) in the range ÷ jobs completed in the range (by completion time).
formula.repeat_rate: Among the customers with at least one job confirmed in the range, the share with at least two jobs confirmed before the range's end.
formula.gmv: What customers were charged (the job's set price plus tax) for the jobs confirmed in the range. A job paid out through a dispute's release was never confirmed and is not counted.
formula.revenue_net_of_refunds: The fee the platform keeps. On the jobs confirmed in the range: its fee as set at payment. On the problems an admin resolved in the range: all of the fee for a release, its part of a split, nothing for a full refund. GMV counts the confirmed jobs only.
